classification_reasons: The only instruction is to sit on the bike and adjust the seat height, which describes setup and not a pedaling movement.
The frames show a man fastening a bike helmet chinstrap and a hand adjusting a seat-post quick-release. Neither frame shows riding or any exertion path.

Bicycling could be represented as a closed-chain, alternating, duration-based leg exercise. But the type of bike, riding posture, resistance, and whether pedaling is intended all change the joint actions, and none of these are given.
Source text and images show only setup and do not demonstrate the exercise named Bicycling, so a faithful kinematic definition cannot be proposed.
questions_requiring_context: Is this meant to be pedaling on a road/mountain bike or a stationary bike, and should it be recorded as duration?
What riding posture is intended (seated upright, seated forward-leaning on handlebars, or standing out of the saddle)?
Should the definition cover steady seated pedaling at moderate resistance, or climbing or sprinting with higher hip and knee demands?
Is the bicycle exercise the pedaling itself, or just the setup shown (helmet and seat adjustment)?
